blocks.content: Quiz: You use a state variable called page inside useEffect() to build the API URL, but you forget to add it to the dependency array. What happens?
Tap an option below to answer:
React automatically detects the missing dependency and adds it
React warns about missing dependencies in development, but it does not add them for you.
React warns about missing dependencies in development, but it does not add them for you.
The effect always reads the initial value of page, ignoring later changes
The effect closes over the initial value and never sees updates. This is called a stale closure.
The effect closes over the initial value and never sees updates. This is called a stale closure.
The effect re-runs every time page changes anyway
Without page in the dependency array, React has no way to know it should re-run.
Without page in the dependency array, React has no way to know it should re-run.
The component throws an error when page changes
React won't throw an error. It silently uses the stale value, which is exactly what makes this bug so hard to spot.
React won't throw an error. It silently uses the stale value, which is exactly what makes this bug so hard to spot.
